name: Brazilian Integralism
summary: Brazilian Integralism is the doctrine of the Ação Integralista Brasileira (AIB), founded by Plínio Salgado in 1932 under the motto God, Fatherland and Family. It sought an Integral State that replaces liberal democracy and political parties with representation through professional classes, corporations, families and municipalities, harmonises capital and labour under state supervision, nationalises strategic services and spreads small property, rejecting both liberal capitalism and communism. It is spiritualist and Catholic in inspiration, defines the Brazilian nation as a fusion of all races to be culturally assimilated, and carried a strong antisemitic strand led by Gustavo Barroso.
scope: The AIB's doctrine from its founding in October 1932 to its dissolution under the Estado Novo (1937-38), as the defining scholarship presents it (Klein s17, Lesser s18, Gonçalves s2/s3, Moraes s4): the October 1932 Manifesto, the AIB's Statutes, Diretrizes and Cartilha, the 1936 Manifesto-Programa, and the 1930s writings of its three doctrinaires, Plínio Salgado, Miguel Reale and Gustavo Barroso. It excludes Salgado's postwar Partido de Representação Popular and the neo-integralist groups, and other countries' integralisms. The AIB never held state power, so the profile rests on its words.

sources.title: Diretrizes Integralistas
sources.author: Ação Integralista Brasileira (Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Doctrinal guidelines: hierarchy of the spiritual over the national, individual subordinate to the community, indissoluble family, family wage and vote, education, state supervision of media, concordat, nationalisations, corporative vote, political centralisation. The archive's copy is a later edition (it cites the 1934 Constitution and mentions television).

sources.title: Estatutos da Ação Integralista Brasileira, art. 3 (1935)
sources.author: Ação Integralista Brasileira, II Congress, Petrópolis (Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Aims of the AIB: God, fatherland and family, national unity, order and authority, social justice, corporations, property limited by the common good, natural resources, armed forces, no struggles between races or classes.

sources.title: Cartilha do Integralismo Brasileiro (1933)
sources.author: Miguel Reale (rapporteur), with Plínio Salgado, João Leães Sobrinho and J. Canuto Mendes de Almeida; archive copy with Reale's 1936 revisions (Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Catechism of the doctrine: state above classes, corporative representation, no parties, unions under the state, labour courts, property and its dissemination, nationalisations, free medical care, schooling, control of press and cinema, against liberalism and bolshevism.

sources.title: Manifesto-Programa de 1936
sources.author: Plínio Salgado, Ação Integralista Brasileira (doctrinal sections; Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: 1936 programme: freedom of conscience and concordat, corporations as the popular will, economic plans and distribution of property, armed forces, South American unity, judiciary, right and duty of work, arts and press.

sources.title: Estado Totalitário e Estado Integral
sources.author: Plínio Salgado (A Offensiva, 1 November 1936; Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: The Integral State as a state of law that does not absorb person, family, economy or religion; doctrine on sedition and the use of force.

sources.title: Nacional-Socialismo e Nacionalismo Cristão
sources.author: Plínio Salgado (A Offensiva, 14 February 1936; Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Salgado's rejection of Nazi racism, the deification of the Führer and sterilisation, and his Christian foundation for the movement.

sources.title: O Integralismo e os Judeus
sources.author: Miguel Reale (A Offensiva, 13 December 1934; Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Reale's rejection of the racist thesis, the fusion of all ethnicities in Brazil, and his conditional stance toward Jews and 'international banking'.

sources.title: O que é o Integralismo
sources.author: Gustavo Barroso (O que o Integralista deve saber, 1935; Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Barroso's account: doctrine not programme, corporative state, rejection of terrorism and sabotage, renunciation and simplicity, corruption of the regime, foreign loans, inner revolution, reason under God.

sources.title: O Estado Corporativo
sources.author: Gustavo Barroso (Espírito do Século XX, 1936; Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Corporative state: unions as natural organs, capital, labour and technique in harmony, rejection of universal suffrage, municipal-provincial-national indirect election, Senate of intellectual professions.

sources.title: Como é a Revolução Integralista (O modus da Revolução)
sources.author: Gustavo Barroso (Espírito do Século XX, 1936; Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Revolution by doctrine and example, peaceful conquest, regeneration of individuals rather than laws.

sources.title: Carta Brasileira do Trabalho
sources.author: Gustavo Barroso, written at Plínio Salgado's order for the AIB Supreme Council (Frente Integralista Brasileira archive, Wayback copy)
sources.usedFor: Labour charter: property as natural right with duties, family, dignity of the person, harmony of capital and labour, right and duty of work, collective contracts, labour magistracy, just and family wage, planned economy.

sources.title: Our Brazil Will Awake! The Acção Integralista Brasileira and the Failed Quest for a Fascist Order in the 1930s

sources.usedFor: History and doctrine of the AIB: fascist identification, the Chefe Nacional's powers, the 1935 turn to legality, race and miscegenation, assimilation of immigrants, the campaign against Japanese immigration, antisemitism, women, minimum wage.

notes: Later pass (rules 5) by claude-opus-5-5. The first pass rested on Wikipedia and an excerpt of the Manifesto; this pass read the full October 1932 Manifesto, the Statutes, Diretrizes, Cartilha and 1936 Manifesto-Programa, and 1934-37 texts by Salgado, Reale and Barroso (archived copies from the Frente Integralista Brasileira site, read through the Wayback Machine because the live site's certificate chain does not verify), plus Klein's CEDLA monograph and Lesser's encyclopedia entry. Every first-pass answer was rechecked; those the sources do not settle are nulled. The AIB never governed, so answers rest on its words; its 1938 putsch and paramilitary militia are not counted as an ideology's record. The Diretrizes copy is a later edition, and the Cartilha copy folds in Reale's 1936 revisions. Barroso's antisemitic books (e.g. Brasil, colônia de banqueiros) were not available; the antisemitic strand is answered from Klein and Reale. Themes searched: economy (property, corporations, unions, wages, nationalisation, credit, planning), government (representation, parties, federalism, head of state, rule of law), society (family, divorce, religion, education, race, immigration, women), world (South American unity, foreign capital, communism, fascism) and means (revolution, force, legality). Ecology, technology and most world questions (alliances, the UN, war) stay null: the sources say nothing on them. Postwar PRP texts on the same archive were not used.
